alex: CI alert on PR #10123 — microbench kv_prefetch_latency increased +9.7% vs baseline (threshold 5%). Link: https://ci.redwood/example/10123/bench/kv_prefetch_latency
ci-bot: PR #10123 — microbench kv_prefetch_latency: baseline 12.3ms -> current 13.5ms (+9.7%). Failing tests: microbench/kv_prefetch_latency, microbench/batch_wait_time. Artifacts: /artifacts/10123 :rotating_light:
maria: oof. Wasn't this PR the kernel-selector refactor? @sam did we expect any perf changes?
sam: It's the kernel-selector + kv prefetch change. I ran the unit bench locally on staging and can reproduce ~+8-10% on long-tail sequences. Command I used:
```
./tools/run_microbench --bench kv_prefetch_latency --commit 6b8f3a
```
lee: profiler dump shows increased memcpy on KV prefetch and a fallback to slower matmul kernel (mm_gemm_fallback). Looks like kernel heuristics now prefer the fallback for seq_len>=384 when batch_size fluctuates. Uploading perf flame: https://artifacts/ci/10123/perf.data
maria: Could be kv prefetch thrashing cache. If prefetch increases KV evictions, cache hitrate drops -> more memops -> slower kernel selection path. Can we bisect between 6a2f9c and 6b8f3a ?
sam: Started a git bisect across the PR range. First suspect commit: 6b8f3a -> kernel-selector heuristic change. Local bisect shows delta appears exactly when we enable the `prefer_sparse_gemm` flag.
dave: If that's the flag, a quick mitigation is revert it or gate behind config. I'll open revert PR and run full CI. If revert fixes CI we can iterate on heuristic offline.
ci-bot: @dave Revert PR #10125 opened: revert prefer_sparse_gemm flag. Running microbench suite.
ci-bot: microbench results (after revert): kv_prefetch_latency back to baseline 12.4ms (+0.8%). Looks like revert fixed the delta. :white_check_mark:
maria: Great. Follow up: collect flamegraphs and add a regression test for seq_len=384/512 patterns to avoid future noise. Also add a small stress test for KV hitrate under prefetch.
sam: Agree. I'll draft a postmortem and follow-up PR that gates the flag by a per-workload estimator instead of a global switch.
alex: Thanks everyone. Marking PR #10123 as blocked on follow-ups. We'll do a canary rollout once the estimator is ready.
